maya: quick question — we're designing the 'slim' header negotiation for model/version selection. thinking of a minimal surface: Accept-Model (model[@version]) + fallback policy query param. who has concerns about backward compatibility?
omar: prefer keeping server default behavior unchanged. any header should be opt-in so existing clients don't break.
lucy: +1. also we need a deprecation timeline plan if we flip defaults later. suggest: opt-in header -> telemetry window -> toggle default -> 90-day deprecation notice.
maya: proposed header semantics:
```
Accept-Model: redwood/base-llm@v2
X-Model-Fallback: base-llm@v1
```
server tries explicit model+version; if unavailable, use X-Model-Fallback; if not present, use current default.
chris: small nit — X-Model-Fallback feels custom. what about fallback=header param or `Accept-Model: redwood/base-llm@v2; fallback=previous` ? keep it single header for less parsing.
omar: agree on single header with param. also need a clear server-side logging field so we can count opt-ins and fallback occurrences. add `Negotiation-Outcome` metric to traces.
lucy: for rollout safety: 1) create flag to treat header as advisory only (no default change), 2) route a sample of traffic to strict-accept behavior for 7 days, 3) gather quality/regression evals, 4) announce default flip with 90d deprecation window.
maya: telemetry keys: AcceptModelRequested, AcceptModelServed, AcceptModelFallbacked, AcceptModelErrored.Anyone object?
chris: no objection. add a short circuit: if header version unknown -> 400? or 422? I'd rather 422 with explanation in body to avoid silent fallback to wrong model.
omar: hmm that could break clients. fallback to default + warning header might be safer to avoid noise. we can surface a deprecation header like `Warning: Unrecognized model param` for dev clients.
lucy: dev-friendly: fallback + Warning header + log an error at rate-limited level. Also add an opt-in strict mode via query param `?strict_model=true` for integration tests.
maya: makes sense. can we doc example for SDKs quickly? e.g., curl + node: 
```
# curl
curl -H "Accept-Model: redwood/base-llm@v2; fallback=previous" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
\n// node
const res = await client.generate({ prompt, headers: { "Accept-Model": "redwood/base-llm@v2; fallback=previous" } });
```
chris: PR checklist: update runtime header parser, add Negotiation-Outcome tracing, add Warning header implementation, add tests for unknown-version behavior, and update SDK docs.
omar: I'll own the runtime parser change (assigning to infra sprint). lucy — can you handle rollout doc + deprecation timeline note for product comms?
lucy: yep, will draft and sync with comms. target doc by EOW.
maya: I'll do the SDK snippets and add a short migration guide.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job for header-negotiation will run tomorrow 03:30 UTC.
omar: thanks. final Q: what is our safe deprecation window if we eventually change default model? lucy: 90 days + migrations playbook (client pin snippets + rollback steps). record that in doc.
maya: labeling action items: [omar] runtime parser + tracing, [lucy] rollout & comms doc, [maya] SDK snippets & migration guide, [chris] tests + PR review.
omar: I'll open the runtime PR today with draft parser and tests.
lucy: will ping legal for any compliance notes for private customers.
maya: great. tl;dr: opt-in header, fallback-friendly default, warn+log unknown versions, telemetry, staged rollout, 90d deprecation window. ping if you want to discuss edge cases.
